pin.how: sha256 over the sorted '<slug>\t<per-work sha256>\n' lines of data/corpus/*.jsonl; independent of the catalog's columns and of where the bytes are hosted

held_layouts.reason: Truncated right-column cells coexist with a full right-column transcription. The exact occurrence association and treatment of partial readings require a separate fragment review.
The OCR combines full column text with partial repeated column snippets. A cell permutation would retain duplicate word occurrences; fragment-level source association is required.
The right-column snippets repeat parts of a later full transcription of that column. Their truncated readings remain contrary evidence; a permutation alone cannot deduplicate their votes.

dubner_reading_review.qualification: Reading-disagreement slots are not an OCR error count or an accuracy rate. The orthographic-only category folds case, combining marks, final sigma, and elision using the frozen alignment key. The one-group count overlaps the other three categories. All contrary readings remain available; unreviewed spellings are not certified.
reopen_when: A source capture or occurrence anchor is invalidated; remove this layer by literal undo before replacing its authority.
A new source review establishes exact fragment identities on a held partial-duplicate page; admit it in a separate reversible layer without another vote group.
New occurrence-specific scan evidence resolves a remaining reading; preserve its contrary readings and original locus in a later review.
dubner_reading_review.review_scope: All ten delimiter-bearing candidate pages were inspected in both scans. Seven exact cell permutations exhaust the approved layout decisions; three partial duplicate-column cases have no admitted fragment decision.

quality.per_work: data/corpus_catalog.tsv carries each work's source, correction status, unattested-token rate and sha256; quality is uneven by work and should be read there

measurement_limits: No assessable systematic-loss case was observed; this run cannot estimate sensitivity or recall.
No assessable page was flagged; this run cannot estimate positive predictive precision.

operating_limits: Counts alone cannot distinguish damaged polytonic text from intentional monotonic or all-capital orthography.
Sparse pages and pages with too little base-letter alignment need a source review rather than a diacritic-loss label.
Character-level reference order is checked separately; text-order errors are not diacritic loss.
This fixed sample is bounded by the available editions and does not establish corpus-wide error rates.
polytonic_loss.scope: Review candidates from OCR sources, grouped by recoverable physical page and witness. A flag is not proof of damaged text. This report never selects a model, changes text, or admits a correction.

legacy_homogeneous_work_bucket.scope: Catalog work-level classification for homogeneous OCR/digital works only; not a global raw-OCR upper bound.

raw_ocr.what: Exact OCR component denominator, with legacy work classification retained separately. Component correction coverage is not inferred from a dominant edition or a local correction stamp.

source_components.counting_basis: Greek regex runs in the checked frequency projection: shared collated attestations count once; unresolved, damaged, restored, and incomplete readings are excluded where explicit lexical eligibility is supplied

apollonius-geom.conica.correction_scope: Source, edition and license describe components. Correction stamps do not establish correction coverage of another component; mixed OCR/digital works have no assessed whole-work correction status.

cassius-dio.historiae-romanae.correction_scope: Source, edition and license describe components. Correction stamps do not establish correction coverage of another component; mixed OCR/digital works have no assessed whole-work correction status.

pappus-mathematics.synagoge.correction_scope: Source, edition and license describe components. Correction stamps do not establish correction coverage of another component; mixed OCR/digital works have no assessed whole-work correction status.

photius.bibliotheca.correction_scope: Source, edition and license describe components. Correction stamps do not establish correction coverage of another component; mixed OCR/digital works have no assessed whole-work correction status.

source_components.scope: Source, edition and license describe components. Correction stamps do not establish correction coverage of another component; mixed OCR/digital works have no assessed whole-work correction status.

hesychius_missing_columns.lexical_count_policy: A scalar lexical reading requires both independent checkpoint groups. Printed editorial or reference scopes, suspect lemmas, and unresolved readings are excluded. Literal predictions and contrary readings remain available. The word projection supplies no context n-grams or positional evidence.
hesychius_missing_columns.qualification: Recovery of the two missing main-text columns from independent Harvard and Ghent copies of the same public-domain 1867 edition. Two pinned OCR checkpoints transcribe each column from both physical copies; outputs from one checkpoint share one vote group. Contrary readings remain explicit and unresolved readings do not enter scalar lexical counts. The literal predictions, both full-page images, title pages, and neighboring boundaries remain auditable. The printed COD./HES. apparatus below the main columns is outside this bounded addition; it remains visible in retained full-page source evidence. Critical signs and Latin citations are not lexical observations, and no context n-grams are inferred from the alignment projection.

remaining_reading_uncertainty.count_basis: Unresolved exact-word alignment slots and singly supported readings in the two recovered main-text columns. These are not OCR error counts or an error rate.

pindar_duplicate_primaries.lexical_count_policy: Exact duplicate serializations of one digital edition contribute one primary occurrence. Canonical primary bytes remain unchanged; original text, citations, source licenses, and retired identifiers remain available.
pindar_duplicate_primaries.qualification: Four duplicate serializations of the same First1K edition are counted once. Equality is exact after removing only the work urn. No Greek text, source license, original citation, or opaque identifier is discarded; the duplicate IDs remain separate retired ledger entries with explicit canonical redirects, rather than being reassigned to another expression.

westermann_source_scope.lexical_count_policy: Only source-supported historical primary units contribute lexical counts. Comparative witnesses of material already represented in a primary, modern editorial text, and held ambiguous text remain outside those counts. Every original row and exact character partition remains reversible.
westermann_source_scope.qualification: Printed work and editorial boundaries repair the historical whole-volume assignment. Every original row and exact character range remains available. Historical material already represented in another primary is comparative, not another lexical occurrence. Ambiguous text roles remain outside primary counts. This source-scope review does not certify unreviewed OCR spellings.

source.qualification: The printed attribution is retained, including anonymous and bracketed attributions. Printed biography subjects are not assigned authorship. This is one edition and one scan, not multiple independent witnesses.

caveats: Sampling stratifies by route and reweights to the overlay, so the corpus figure is not the sample average: freq/accepted holds 72,856 records and agent/accepted 1,376, and both were sampled to the same depth.
9.6% of items are neither sound nor wrong but a split or unsure reading, and are reported as their own band rather than rounded into either side.
The two raters disagree on 5.5% of items, so no figure here is finer than a few points.
The estimate counts corrections that are wrong, not OCR errors that survive: a raw-OCR work has had no correction pass at all and none of these rates say anything about it.
llm/accepted's 74.0% is a sample of the 1,654 records left after its census reverted 868 unanimously wrong records.
prosodia/accepted (682 records) and engine/accepted (4) were below the sampling floor and are not covered by any figure here.
The per-work unattested_rate in data/corpus_catalog.tsv is a triage signal, not a character error rate: a lexicon or a dialect glossary scores high on rare vocabulary without being misread.

censused_by_corrector.raters: two independent agent instances of one model family, each shown the passage, both forms and the corrector's note, with no verdict, corrector or status. Agreement is therefore a reproducibility bound and not evidence of correctness: a blind spot the model shares passes both raters
censused_by_corrector.split_still_applied: a census gate is asymmetric on purpose: it reverts only where both raters call a record wrong, because a bad correction left in place is a measured defect while a reverted good one is fresh OCR damage in text that was right. So the records the raters disagreed on stay in the served text, 11,296 of them across the five cells, and 7,012 of those carry at least one wrong verdict. That is the censuses' own residual and it is not counted in any rate above: read sound, reverted and this as three bands, not two
censused_by_corrector.what: both-raters-right over every staged record of the cell, read one at a time rather than sampled; `reverted` is the records both raters called wrong, which are out of the served text. agent/accepted has not been censused and rests on the sample above

survivor_precision.evidence: data/precision/gate_verify_eustathius_*/ and data/precision/gate_verify_collation_proposed/ in the upstream pipeline
survivor_precision.what: a second blind two-rater read of a random sample of the records the census KEPT, which is what the bake actually wrote; the cells themselves read 83.8%, 92.1% and 86.3%. Read it as reproducibility rather than truth, since the second pair shares a model family with the first

history_since_2026_08_12.what: seven bakes after the original 2026-08-12 sample and before the current 2026-09-13 sample. The 2026-08-21 Eustathius bake: 16,570 records against the Iliad commentary said auto or accepted while the rows still held the OCR reading, so nothing had ever been applied. All 16,601 staged proposals were read by two blind raters across two gates, freq/auto (16,081 read) and confusion/accepted (520); 2,651 were rejected and 13,959 written, plus 58 active records elsewhere that had gone unapplied. The 2026-09-11 collation bake: OCR readings a census revert had put back in the text, corrected again by collation against an independent digital text of the same work, which supplies the letters while case, movable nu, rho breathing and final accent follow this edition's own usage. All 2,400 proposals were read by two blind raters who were not told where they came from, and only the 2,072 both called right were written. A 105-record rebake restored census collateral after duplicate-edit cleanup. Four upstream OCR-frequency correction batches then wrote 16,097 independently evidenced corrections

legacy_homogeneous_work_stamp_gap.scope: Bounds within the homogeneous works classified raw by the catalog; not global raw-OCR bounds. Mixed-component correction coverage is unassessed.
legacy_homogeneous_work_stamp_gap.what: row-and-method pairs where an active correction is standing in the served row and the row carries no stamp for that method, because a carve moved the row after apply_corrections.py stamped it

wrong_corrections.method: two independent blind raters per item over a random sample of the served overlay, stratified by the route that applied each correction; a correction counts sound only when both raters call it right and wrong only when both call it wrong

overlay_reach.caveats: `placed` is weaker than `present`: 641 of the placed records land on a row that does not carry the correction. 16 of the convention placements are undecidable, because a row split at a character offset leaves both halves carrying the form. The 23,550 point at text this corpus keeps but does not serve as the primary reading: a second witness under data/corpus_secondary, a leaf dropped as a repeat of another with the audit naming the twin that kept it, Migne's apparatus in data/paratext, or a row an audit archived verbatim
overlay_reach.what: where the active records sit relative to the served text. A record keyed to a row a carve moved is not lost: the carve audits, or the convention that a carved row keeps its Migne page identity, place most of them

repaired_over_reverts.evidence: data/corrections/over_revert_repair_*.json in the upstream pipeline, each carrying the row before and after and the commit the fix was applied at
repaired_over_reverts.what: tokens a revert overwrote although no correction had ever made them. 1,047 of the rows come from the wholesale llm/accepted revert of 2026-08-02 and the rest from the gated census payouts; the worst single row had eleven ordinary καὶ rewritten as Κἢ. No correction record changed, because these are positions no record named

reverted_since_measurement.audits: data/corrections/cell_revert_*.json in the upstream pipeline, whose record lists sum to these figures
reverted_since_measurement.what: the complete llm/auto census payout after the 2026-09-13 sample: 7,640 unanimously wrong edit keys plus one duplicate active record carrying a condemned edit. The three payout audits hold 4,459, 2,059 and 1,123 records. The wrong_rows_estimate above describes the overlay before those reverts; subtracting them leaves roughly 12,700 estimated wrong records, with split and unsure verdicts deliberately retained

superseded.why: those samples were drawn per corrector from slices chosen for being hard and mostly rested on n around 30 with one rater; compared one-rater to one-rater every cell but llm/auto was optimistic by 6 to 8 points
